items.text: Understand that permission boundaries set a ceiling — they never grant permissions
Explain effective permissions = intersection of identity policy and permission boundary
Distinguish session policies (per-call) from permission boundaries (standing/durable)
Recite the IAM three-step evaluation: Explicit Deny → Explicit Allow → Implicit Deny
Explain the cross-account two-policy handshake (STS:AssumeRole + trust policy)
Identify which policies govern a session after role assumption (role's policies, not caller's)
Explain the Confused Deputy problem and how External ID prevents it
Differentiate aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent (session boolean) from aws:MultiFactorAuthAge (seconds, for freshness)
List the nine AWS services that support resource-based policies
Explain why IAM groups cannot be principals in resource-based policies
Identify the source account and destination account in any cross-account scenario
Determine whether a permission boundary on a user applies during role assumption (it does NOT)
Design the correct control placement: boundary on the role, not the assuming user
Choose between aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent and aws:MultiFactorAuthAge for a given security requirement
Debug cross-account KMS-encrypted S3 access failures in the correct four-step order
Identify when a session policy vs a permission boundary solves a scenario
Recognize the KMS two-pronged authorization requirement (role policy AND KMS key policy)
Answer SAA-C03 questions on permission boundary behavior without confusing it with session policies
Identify Confused Deputy scenarios and select External ID as the solution
Select the correct MFA condition key (Age vs Present) for session hijacking defense questions
Correctly identify source vs destination account in cross-account scenario questions
Answer 'select two' questions combining Confused Deputy + per-call scoping mechanisms
Recognize that explicit deny in ANY policy overrides ALL allows — same account or cross-account
Recall that SMS MFA was deprecated in 2019 for new configurations
Apply the four IAM security mechanisms (floor/ceiling/gate/contextual gate) to multi-requirement scenarios
